subject: pathology
title: Vaso-Occlusive Crisis, Beta Thalassaemia Major, and Haemoglobin Analysis

steps.tx: Vaso-occlusive crisis begins when sickled cells, activated endothelium, leucocytes, and platelets jam postcapillary venules, infarcting marrow, bone, and viscera with pain out of proportion to signs. Dactylitis in toddlers and bone pain later are its dialects; the event is a **vaso-occlusive crisis**.
steps.say: Vaso-occlusive pain is microvascular infarction; treat pain fast, hunt infection, and hydrate judiciously.

steps.tx: Acute chest syndrome, new pulmonary infiltrate with fever, hypoxia, and chest pain, is the crisis that kills adults, driven by infection, fat embolism from infarcted marrow, and in situ sickling. Oxygen, antibiotics, transfusion strategy, and incentive spirometry treat **acute chest syndrome**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Fever, hypoxia, and a new chest infiltrate in sickle disease mean acute chest syndrome; act before it escalates.

steps.tx: Beta thalassaemia major abolishes beta chain production, leaving alpha chains to precipitate inside precursors, destroying marrow output and expanding bones while transfusions load iron into heart and liver. Cooley anaemia is its historic name; the disease is **beta thalassaemia major**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: No beta chains means alpha precipitation, ineffective erythropoiesis, bone expansion, and transfusion iron overload.

vis.caption: Thalassaemia pathology with ineffective erythropoiesis and expanded marrow spaces.

steps.tx: Fetal haemoglobin rescues newborns with beta thalassaemia until gamma chains switch off around six months, after which anaemia deepens and transfusions begin, while raised HbF in hereditary persistence softens disease. The protective fraction is **haemoglobin F (HbF, alpha2 gamma2)**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: HbF hides beta thalassaemia for six months and sickle disease for longer; its fall unmasks both.

rows: Minor adult fraction, raised in beta trait

steps.tx: Raised HbA2 above three and a half percent with microcytosis and normal iron stores is the laboratory signature of beta thalassaemia trait, vital to detect before couples plan pregnancies. The trait marker is **raised HbA2 in beta thalassaemia trait**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Microcytosis with normal iron and HbA2 above three and a half percent equals beta thalassaemia trait.

steps.tx: Haemoglobin electrophoresis separates fractions by charge at alkaline pH, while HPLC quantifies them precisely and resolves variants that co-migrate, together forming the diagnostic bench for every haemoglobinopathy. The quantifying method is **high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Electrophoresis separates, HPLC quantifies; together they name every haemoglobinopathy precisely.

steps.tx: Transfusion programmes in thalassaemia major suppress ineffective erythropoiesis and permit growth, but each unit adds iron no physiology can excrete, so chelation with deferasirox or pumps guards heart and endocrine organs. The balancing act is **transfusion and iron chelation therapy**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Transfuse to suppress the marrow, chelate to save the heart; thalassaemia major care is that balance for life.

steps.tx: Stroke prevention in sickle childhood uses transcranial Doppler velocities to select chronic transfusion, while exchange transfusion treats acute stroke, severe acute chest, and multiorgan failure. Knowing when simple top up suffices versus exchange is **sickle transfusion decision making**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Doppler velocities select children for stroke prevention transfusion; exchange rescues stroke and severe acute chest.
